skill.name: finishing-branches
skill.description: Guides branch completion with CI checks, secret scans, change review, pull request creation, and post-merge cleanup commands.
skill.summary: Finish development branches with checks, PR preparation, and cleanup steps.
skill.author: BPSAI

security_audit.summary: The static backtick findings are false positives because they point to Markdown code fences, not executable Ruby or shell interpolation. One semantic risk remains: the workflow includes PR creation, branch deletion, broad staging, committing, and pushing, which require explicit user confirmation. No prompt injection language or secret exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: State-changing repository commands are presented as direct workflow steps.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before PR creation, branch deletion, commits, pushes, or broad staging. Split the quick finish chain into reviewable steps.

remediation.issue: The quick finish flow stages all files before committing and pushing.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to review changed files and run the secret scan before staging, committing, and pushing branch contents.

semantic_findings.title: State-Changing Git Workflow Commands
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends automatic PR creation, branch deletion, broad staging, committing, and pushing. If an agent runs these steps without explicit confirmation, it can publish unintended changes or remove local branch state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines clearly include repository-mutating operations. The impact depends on whether the host agent asks before running them, so medium severity is appropriate.

content.value_statement: Finishing a branch often requires checks, review, PR notes, and cleanup. This skill provides a repeatable workflow for safe branch completion.
actual_capabilities: Lists CI and validation checks to run before merge.
Prompts a staged secret scan before pull request creation.
Guides review of branch changes against the main branch.
Provides a pull request template with summary, testing, and checklist sections.
Documents post-merge cleanup commands for local branches.
Offers a compact quick finish command sequence for advanced users.
limitations: Depends on the bpsai-pair CLI being installed and configured.
Assumes a Git workflow that uses a main branch.
Does not verify test results or pull request content independently.
Quick finish commands can stage unintended files if used without review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Feature Branch for Review
use_cases.description: Run final checks, inspect changes, scan for secrets, and assemble pull request notes before asking for review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team PR Readiness
use_cases.description: Use the same checklist for testing, documentation, task status, and review quality across team branches.

use_cases.title: Clean Up After Merge
use_cases.description: Return to the main branch, pull the latest changes, and remove merged local branches after confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Finish My Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the finishing-branches skill to guide me through final checks before I create a pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare PR Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me review my current branch and draft pull request notes using the finishing-branches checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the finishing-branches workflow and identify any missing checks before this branch is merged.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Merge Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: After I confirm the merge, use finishing-branches to plan safe local cleanup and branch removal steps.

output_examples.input: I finished TASK-123 and need to open a pull request.
output_examples.output: A pre-merge checklist covering tests, validation, secret scanning, change review, task status, and pull request notes.

output_examples.input: Check whether my branch is ready to merge.
output_examples.output: A readiness review that highlights required checks, missing documentation, debug statements, and unresolved task status.

output_examples.input: The branch has merged. What cleanup remains?
output_examples.output: A short post-merge plan to update the main branch and remove the merged local branch after confirmation.

best_practices: Review the diff before staging or pushing changes.
Run the secret scan before creating a pull request.
Confirm task status and PR notes match the delivered work.
anti_patterns: Using the quick finish flow before inspecting changed files.
Deleting a local branch before confirming the merge.
Treating generated pull request text as final without context review.

faq.question: Does this skill create pull requests automatically?
faq.answer: It documents a workflow that can use a project CLI for pull request creation. Users should confirm before running that step.

faq.question: Can I use it without the bpsai-pair CLI?
faq.answer: Parts of the checklist still apply, but the named project commands require that CLI to be installed.

faq.question: Does it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It prepares a branch for review, but reviewers still need to inspect behavior, tests, and design choices.

faq.question: Does it scan for leaked secrets?
faq.answer: It includes a staged secret scan step. Users should still verify that their project scanner is configured correctly.

faq.question: Is the quick finish flow safe for every branch?
faq.answer: No. It is best for advanced users after checking changed files, test results, and staged content.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
